clue.text: Swaying, rocking action so, bilious on board

indicators.note: being on board means being inside, so the next piece goes within the rearranged letters
rocking shakes things about, so the letters of action and so are rearranged

parts.note: bilious means feeling sick, ill

explanation.surface: Someone describes a nauseating rocking motion, feeling queasy on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures seasickness, but 'on board' is the container signal and 'bilious' just means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaying back-and-forth movement is an oscillation, a regular swing between two positions.

clue.text: Sailor with bad temper in King Edward's smack?

definitions.note: the noun phrase names a flavour, a smack, given to a potato

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
with means and, joining things together
vinegar is sourness or ill temper of manner

explanation.surface: A grumpy sailor appears in a monarch's company, or gets slapped by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety, so its 'smack' (taste) is a crisp or chip flavour; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and vinegar is the classic British seasoning for chips and crisps, the flavour a potato might carry.

clue.text: Flatten metal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to press smooth, as clothes with a hot appliance

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for pressing creases out of clothes and the name of the common metallic element.

clue.text: On welcoming first of invitees, call up vassal

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of invitees

parts.note: first letter of invitees

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a servant once the first guest has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, a convention setters lean on; 'up' works as reversal because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a feudal subject who owed loyalty and service to a lord, just as a vassal did.

clue.text: Artist: Hyperion, for example, inspiring one

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the letter is drawn inside

parts.note: Hyperion was one of the Titans of Greek myth
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An artist cites Hyperion, perhaps Keats's poem, as an example that inspires someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' puts I (one) inside TITAN, Hyperion being one of the Titans.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: More than one animal in buffalo, fox, giraffe and penguin, last of all

indicators.note: last of all takes the final letter of every one of the four animals listed

explanation.surface: A list of zoo creatures with a plural animal tucked among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural of ox, so it names several animals of one kind, cattle.

clue.text: Manoeuvre tricky there, indicate, then go

indicators.note: tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so the letters of there are rearranged

parts.note: to indicate is to point
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A driving instructor's commentary on an awkward manoeuvre: signal, then go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges THERE into THREE; then POINT (indicate) and TURN (go).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the driving move of turning a car round in a narrow road in forward, reverse and forward movements.

clue.text: Tasteless sandwiches put in container on top of doughnuts, sweet

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the following letters go inside

parts.note: a tasteless joke is a sick one
potted means placed in a pot

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of doughnuts

explanation.surface: A bad-taste snack is stored in a tin over some doughnuts, a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A sick joke is a tasteless one. Spotted dick is a British steamed sponge with currants, the 'sweet' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a traditional British steamed suet pudding with currants, so it is a sweet, a dessert.

clue.text: Where merchandise is scattered?

parts.note: an idiom for everywhere in disorder, read literally as goods strewn across a store

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, goods spread throughout a store; the idiom means in a mess, all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everywhere and in disarray, which literally describes stock strewn about a store.

clue.text: Something said by charmer, rogue being cuddled by a couple of supporters?

indicators.note: being cuddled means held inside, so the rogue goes between the two supporters

parts.note: a bra is a supporter, so a couple of them is A BRA twice
a cad is a rogue

explanation.surface: A smooth charmer, a cad, is embraced, held up by a couple of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cuddled by' puts CAD (rogue) between A BRA and A BRA, the 'couple of supporters' (bras support).
explanation.definitionFit: It is the magic word uttered by a conjuror or enchanter casting a spell.

clue.text: Bill educator

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for a schoolteacher, or a magistrate

explanation.definitionFit: A beak is a bird's mouthpart, and old British school slang for a headmaster or teacher.

clue.text: Splendid drink knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: lager is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: A spilled pint looking rather grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, so magnificent or splendid in the manner of royalty.

clue.text: Four characters in Europe standing trial

indicators.note: four characters in points to a run of four letters lying inside the next words

explanation.surface: Someone in Europe is standing trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial in this sense is a nuisance, an annoying person or thing, and a pest is just that.

clue.text: Jar colossal, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: colossal means huge, great

explanation.surface: A huge jar, described as it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container noun; it is the verb, to grate on the nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to have an irritating, harsh effect, which is what grating does.

clue.text: Islander sending up all but two characters in opera

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up means the word is read upwards, backwards
all but two characters means the opera's name loses its last two letters

parts.note: Nabucco is an opera by Verdi

explanation.surface: An islander mocks most of the cast of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Nabucco is Verdi's opera; 'all but two characters' cuts it to NABUC, and 'sending up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban is a native of Cuba, the Caribbean island, so an islander.

clue.text: Resident of small country governed by First Lady, out of bounds

indicators.note: out of bounds means without its outer edges, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Pandora was the first woman in Greek myth
governed means ran, as a country

explanation.surface: A small country ruled by a president's wife who has strayed off-limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' is not a president's wife but PANDORA, the first woman of Greek myth; 'out of bounds' trims her to ANDOR, then RAN (governed).
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality in the Pyrenees, so one of its citizens lives in a small country.

clue.text: Over-elaborate colour

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the hue between red and blue

explanation.definitionFit: Purple describes ornate, overwritten prose and is also the name of a hue mixing red and blue.

clue.text: Transmittable skill of fielders

definitions.meaning: first meaning: infectious, as a disease
second meaning: taking the ball cleanly in cricket or baseball

explanation.definitionFit: A contagious illness is catching, and catching the ball is a core skill of players in the field.

clue.text: Perhaps brief peer is taken inside box that neither opens nor closes

indicators.note: taken inside means placed within, so is goes into the trimmed box
neither opens nor closes means the box loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a carton is a box

explanation.surface: A peer, possibly a judge, is taken into a sealed box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps brief' marks the definition as a shortened word, hence the 'perhaps': aristo is a clipped form.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortened form of aristocrat is a casual word for a nobleman, and a peer is such a nobleman.

clue.text: Primate departs tropical tree

parts.note: a tamarin is a small South American monkey
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A monkey leaves its tree in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a leguminous tree of tropical regions, grown for its sour pods.

clue.text: Case of goliath leading India, anti-colonialist

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so these letters come before the next

parts.note: the case, or outer letters, of goliath are G and H, read literally as G AND H
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A giant figure heading a nation, one who fought empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters of goliath are G and H, and the clue has you write out 'G and H' in full, then put I (India) after.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's non-violent campaign for independence from British colonial rule.

clue.text: Before kiss, take off top

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: to take off is to mimic, to ape
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone removes a top before a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like undressing; it means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point, the peak or summit of something.

clue.text: Lighter twin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stick for lighting fires
second meaning: an identical counterpart, an equal

explanation.definitionFit: A match is a small stick struck for a flame, and also an exact equal or pair to something.

clue.text: On the organ with a drum, our two instruments clashing, initially

definitions.text: On the organ with a drum

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: An organ, a drum and other instruments clash in a noisy performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'organ with a drum' looks musical but is the ear, which has an eardrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic means relating to the ear, the body part that contains the eardrum.

clue.text: Bones, when like that, turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
so means like that, in that way

explanation.surface: Bones flipped over when found like that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for a bone.

clue.text: Final word, acknowledgment by unsuccessful angler?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obituary, the last thing written about someone
second meaning, read cryptically: an angler admitting that nothing, zero, bit

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into O (nothing) and BIT, as a luckless angler might say no fish bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary notice is the last word published on a life, and nought bit is a fishless day.

clue.text: Novel published on Ray, jazz favourite

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A book has come out about Ray, a fan of jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book; it is the signal to rearrange PUBLISHED ON RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's 1924 piece for piano and band is a much-loved jazz-influenced classic.

clue.text: Flag is pentagon, surprisingly divided by five

indicators.note: divided by means split by, so the next letter goes inside
surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters of is and pentagon are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A five-sided paving piece, oddly split into five parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner; it is a flagstone, a flat paving slab.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a flat slab of stone used for paving, a flagstone.
